answer: Each identity joins a grove pool with a 50-credit bond and a per-epoch premium from its own funds. A prism table sorts identities into risk bands by age and claims, charging new identities 12 and a nadir rate of 3 after three clean epochs. Auditors publish payments and claims for public recomputation; a proven fake forfeits its bond. The k-th fake adds 50 bond plus 12 per epoch, so 1,000 fakes lock 50,000 and pay 12,000 per epoch, with no discount. Lapse-and-revive fails: revival charges back premiums plus 10. An honest agent pays 12 for three epochs, then 3.
